newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm but gains capped.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm but gains capped.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher on Monday, backed by bargain hunting on the underlying cash market, but dealers said the gains were made on thin volumes and the upside looked limited.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract added 220 points to end at 20,365 after hitting a high of 20,465 on volume of 10,830 lots.

"I heard there was buying by a (Japanese) fund on the cash market. And we didn't see too many sellers. That's why the market got pushed up on thin volume," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
He said the 20,200 level looked well supported for the time being but there was little immediate reason to buy the Nikkei unless the dollar rose against the yen.
"The market's looking pretty toppish around here. I'd expect some profit-taking near 20,500," a trader with a U.S. house said, adding that the June Nikkei should hold above 20,000.
On Taiwan futures, the June contract ended at 347.4 against its opening 345.5 on volume of 424 lots.
